data.title: Getting to know you; how IELTS works
data.course: HEC IELTS Speaking & Listening · Year 1 · Term 1
data.subtitle: Lesson 1 · 120 minutes
data.bigQuestion: What makes a good first conversation with someone new?
objectives: Introduce yourself and others with three linked details, not single words.
Know the shape of the IELTS Speaking and Listening papers and what examiners listen for.
Hear and mark word stress on two- and three-syllable words.
Answer Part 1 questions with a reason or an example, and score a partner fairly.

blocks.heading: Find someone who…
paragraphs: Students stand and mingle. Each has a card of eight prompts and must find a different classmate for each one, then ask one follow-up question before writing a name.

lists.title: How it runs
items: Model one exchange with a confident student, including the follow-up question.
Give four minutes of mingling; play quiet music and stop it at the end.
Students sit with the classmate they found most surprising and report one fact each.

lists.title: Follow-up questions to model
items: Oh really? How did you get into that?
What do you enjoy most about it?
How long have you been doing it?

blocks.heading: Talking about yourself in three steps
paragraphs: A strong Part 1 answer has three moves: a direct answer, a reason, and a detail or example. Build the pattern on the board, then let pairs practise with the prompts below.

head: Move
Useful language
Example
rows: Yes, I do / Not really / Mostly…
mainly because it helps me relax after school.
Last Sunday I played for two hours with my cousins.

tiers.task: Answer three questions with an answer and a reason, using the frames.
Answer four questions with all three moves. Your partner ticks each move they hear.
Answer, then add a contrast: what was different when you were younger?
frames: When I was younger, I used to…, but now…

blocks.heading: Word stress: where the beat falls

items: Clap the beat of three names in the room; the loud clap is the stressed syllable.
Students sort the words into four stress patterns (Oo, oO, Ooo, oOo): hobby, describe, family, important, weekend, holiday, relax, computer.
Pairs say the words in a sentence of their own; the partner taps the stress.

blocks.heading: Interview practice with peer scoring
paragraphs: One student is the examiner and reads four questions; the other answers. After four minutes they swap. The examiner scores with the checklist and gives one specific piece of praise and one target.

lists.title: Examiner's checklist
items: Answered the question that was asked
Gave a reason with every answer
Added a detail or example at least twice
Spoke for about 15 to 20 seconds each time

tiers.task: Use the question card with picture prompts; answer with two moves.
Answer the four topic questions with three moves, without notes.
Ask your partner one follow-up question of your own after each answer.

blocks.heading: Joining a weekend club
paragraphs: Students hear a short conversation at a sports centre twice. First listening: answer the questions. Second listening: check, then compare with a partner.

questions.title: Questions 1–5
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER, or tick the right box.

items.q: Which activity does she want to join?
What should she bring to the first session?

blocks.heading: This house believes first impressions are usually right
paragraphs: Two teams of four. Each speaker has one minute. Proposition opens, opposition replies, then two minutes of open floor and a one-minute summary from each side.

lists.title: Running order
items: Five minutes of preparation: each team lists three arguments and one example for each.
Speeches alternate: proposition 1, opposition 1, proposition 2, opposition 2.
Open floor: any speaker may stand to challenge a point.
Summaries, then the class votes by moving to one side of the room.

lists.title: Language for debating
items: I'd like to challenge that point.
That may be true, but…
Let me give you an example.
To sum up our case…

tiers.task: Give one argument with one example, reading from your notes.
Give two arguments and answer one challenge from the other team.
Summarise both sides fairly before explaining why yours is stronger.

items: I can introduce myself with three linked details.
I know the four parts of the IELTS Listening test.
I can hear the stressed syllable in a new word.

blocks.heading: This week at home
paragraphs: Short and often is better than long and rare. Each day has one task; tick the box when it is done and bring the sheet next lesson.

head: Day
Task
Minutes
rows: Record a one-minute self-introduction using the three moves.
Listen to the club script again; shadow the caller's lines.
Learn ten words from the topic list; mark the stress.
Write five Part 1 answers (answer, reason, detail).
Prepare one argument for and one against next week's motion.
Talk with a family member for ten minutes in English; note two new words.

tiers.task: Do Monday, Wednesday and Thursday; use the frames sheet.
Also record your Thursday answers and listen for word stress.
